reviewBoundary: Six original junior whole-passage grammar practices, mixing habitual present explanations and past classroom incidents. Fictional demonstrations, no invented empirical study or quantitative result. Same-author structure and alternative-form review; unknown forms reviewable, no independent calibration.

units.title: Seeds beside a window
units.alignmentNote: Complete original ten-gap passage, seven supplied-word gaps plus three one-word gaps. Source supplies level/family reference only.

materials.title: Seeds beside a window
materials.text:
Each spring, our science club ____1____ (grow) a few bean plants beside a classroom window. We begin with seeds on damp paper so that the first roots can be seen. Later, the young plants are moved into pots with suitable soil.

The activity requires regular attention rather ____2____ a single afternoon of work. Someone checks whether the paper remains damp, while another student makes sure the pots have a suitable place to stand. Giving a plant more water is not always ____3____ (good) than giving it the right amount.

Before ____4____ (start), we label the containers. This prevents us from confusing plants that look similar. Our teacher asks us to describe what happens without deciding in advance what we expect to find.

Last year, one group forgot ____5____ (check) its tray over a holiday. Some seedlings dried out. The teacher did not ask us to pretend that every plant had grown equally well. We explained the problem and changed our rota.

Now, the pupil ____6____ is on duty writes a short note before leaving. Other ____7____ (member) can see whether watering has already been done. The notes belong to the whole group, not just the tallest plant's owner.

Watching roots develop gives ____8____ (we) a view of something usually hidden. We do the work ____9____ (careful), but still expect differences among living things. It is ____10____ useful reminder that care means noticing a plant's condition, not simply repeating one action regardless of what happens.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of grow.
questions.explanation: Each spring states a habit. Grows uses singular agreement with club; British notional plural grow can refer to the members and is also accepted. Growing alone lacks a finite auxiliary.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Rather than introduces the contrast with one afternoon. Then is time, as/from do not complete rather.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of good.
questions.explanation: Than requires irregular comparative better. Plain good, superlative best and nonstandard gooder do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of start.
questions.explanation: Before functions as a preposition taking starting. The other forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of check.
questions.explanation: Forgot to check means failed to do the needed check. Forgot checking means lost the memory of having checked, conflicting with the tray drying through an omitted duty.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Who/that is the defining human subject. Which is nonhuman, where not subject and whose needs a possessed noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of member.
questions.explanation: Other members names several group participants. Singular member would need another structure; membership is the status/collection rather than the people reading the notes.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Gives takes object us. Subject and possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Carefully modifies do the work. Careful is adjective and carefulness noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A useful reminder begins with consonant /j/, so a. Unlisted article readings remain reviewable.

materials.title: One note in a handbell group
materials.text:
In our school handbell group, each player ____1____ (hold) one or two bells. A complete tune depends on different people sounding their notes at the correct moment. Owning the loudest bell does not make one person the whole group.

Our teacher begins each rehearsal by asking us ____2____ (listen) to the tune without playing. Then we look at the marks ____3____ show when our own notes are needed. The music may sound simple, but staying silent at the right time matters too.

When I first joined, I rang my bell whenever I felt nervous. That made the tune ____4____ (difficult) to recognise than it should have been. I wanted to show that I was taking part, yet I needed to wait for my turn.

After ____5____ (practise) slowly with a smaller group, I began to hear where my note belonged. A friend helped me count through the rests rather than guessing from the movement of the teacher's hands alone.

At the winter concert, we played a short piece for ____6____ (we) families. I missed one note but did not ring it late and interrupt the next phrase. The teacher had prepared us ____7____ that possibility.

We finished together, and several parents smiled at the final sound. Afterwards, I thanked my friend for explaining the rests so ____8____ (patient). I had learned ____9____ important part of making music: sometimes the right contribution is a little silence. Our bells were separate ____10____ (instrument), but the melody belonged to everyone.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of hold.
questions.explanation: Each player is singular in a habitual present statement: holds. Hold disagrees; holding lacks auxiliary.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of listen.
questions.explanation: Asking us takes to listen. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Marks are subject antecedent of that/which show. Who is human, where not subject and what does not follow this antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of difficult.
questions.explanation: Than requires comparative more difficult. Plain and superlative forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of practise.
questions.explanation: After takes an -ing form; British practising and American practicing are accepted. Base, past and to-infinitive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Our modifies families. We/us are personal pronouns and ours cannot directly precede the noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Prepared us for that possibility uses for. The other prepositions do not complete this preparation construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of patient.
questions.explanation: Patiently modifies explaining. Patient is adjective and patience noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: An important part agrees with the vowel sound. A is incorrect sound agreement; other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of instrument.
questions.explanation: Plural bells were separate instruments. Instrument is singular and instrumental an adjective.

materials.title: Drawing in the gallery
materials.text:
Last month, our art teacher ____1____ (take) us to a small gallery. We were allowed to sketch in pencil, but the staff asked us not to use paint near the pictures. Each student chose one work to study rather than trying to copy the whole room.

I selected a painting of a kitchen ____2____ contained several ordinary objects. At first, I looked only at the bright bowl in the centre. My teacher asked me to notice the spaces around it as well.

Before ____3____ (draw) any details, I marked the main shapes lightly. That made it ____4____ (easy) to change their positions than it would have been after adding dark lines. The teacher did not tell us to make exact copies. She wanted us to understand how the parts worked together.

A visitor stopped nearby and looked at my sketch. I felt nervous, but she simply asked which picture I had chosen. I pointed ____5____ the kitchen painting, and she noticed a small spoon I had missed.

At the end of the visit, our ____6____ (drawing) were all different. Some showed careful outlines; others used only a few shapes. We talked ____7____ (quiet) so that we would not disturb the other visitors.

I decided ____8____ (keep) the sketch beside a postcard of the painting. It was not ____9____ perfect copy, but it reminded me of what I had looked at. The spoon added by a stranger's question became my favourite detail. That small exchange helped ____10____ (I) see the picture again.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of take.
questions.explanation: Last month requires irregular past took. Take is base/present and taked nonstandard.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: The painting is subject antecedent of that/which contained. Where would leave contained without a subject; who is human and what does not fit an expressed antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of draw.
questions.explanation: Before takes drawing as the non-finite prepositional complement. Other forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of easy.
questions.explanation: Than requires comparative easier/more easy. Plain, superlative and doubled comparative forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Pointed to/at/toward(s) can all identify the painting. Of and from do not identify the indicated target here.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of drawing.
questions.explanation: Our separate works with were all different are plural drawings. Drawing is singular and drawn a participle.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of quiet.
questions.explanation: Quietly modifies talked. Quietness is noun; an informal flat-adverb reading is left reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of keep.
questions.explanation: Decided takes to keep. Other listed forms do not complete it.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A perfect copy uses a before a consonant sound. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of I.
questions.explanation: Helped takes object me before see. I is subject and my/mine possessive.

materials.title: A box that used sunlight
materials.text:
Our science club built a simple demonstration cooker from a box and reflective material. We did not expect it ____1____ (replace) an ordinary kitchen. The purpose was to explore how sunlight could warm a small enclosed space.

Our teacher checked the design and supervised each trial. We placed a thermometer inside rather than using our fingers to guess the temperature. The instrument ____2____ (read) at regular intervals, and the time was written beside each result.

One afternoon, clouds covered the sun halfway through the activity. The temperature stopped rising as ____3____ (quick) as before. Instead of deleting that part of the record, we noted the change in the weather.

A classmate suggested ____4____ (compare) our results with another group's. Their box was a different size, however, so we could not treat the sunlight as the only possible cause of any difference. Our teacher asked us to identify the conditions ____5____ had changed.

The discussion was more interesting than simply deciding which of the day’s readings was the ____6____ (high). We considered what our trial could show and where it left questions unanswered.

At the next meeting, we agreed ____7____ a smaller question to investigate. That helped ____8____ (we) make a clearer plan. The box was still a modest classroom model, not evidence that every cooking task could be done in the same way. It had become ____9____ useful tool for asking questions. We learned to describe our work ____10____ (careful), including the conditions that made each observation possible.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of replace.
questions.explanation: Expect it takes to replace. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of read.
questions.explanation: The singular instrument receives readings in the trial narrative. Was read/had been read are passive. Read alone lacks auxiliary and were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of quick.
questions.explanation: Quickly modifies rising in as quickly as. Quickness is a noun; a flat-adverb quick reading remains reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of compare.
questions.explanation: Suggested directly takes comparing. Other listed forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Conditions are subject antecedent of that/which had changed. Who is human, where not subject and what does not fit this antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of high.
questions.explanation: Which of the day’s readings was the highest ranks the maximum. Higher is only comparative and most highest doubles the superlative. Other possible unlisted readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Agreed on/upon a question means jointly selected it. Of and at do not complete agree here. Other unlisted readings, including an approval construction with to, remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Helped takes object us. Subject and possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A useful tool uses consonant /j/. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Carefully modifies describe. Careful and carefulness are adjective/noun.

materials.title: A forecast on the school noticeboard
materials.text:
Every morning, a member of our geography club ____1____ (prepare) a short weather notice. It combines the forecast for the area with observations made at school. The two sources are clearly labelled because they do not describe exactly the same thing.

A forecast concerns what may happen later, while an observation reports a condition at a particular time. Someone ____2____ reads our notice should be able to tell which kind of information each sentence gives.

We use simple language rather than ____3____ (copy) long technical descriptions. However, making the wording shorter should not make an uncertain forecast sound definite. A chance of rain does not mean that rain has already started.

Last week, our morning report said the sky was clear. By lunchtime, clouds had arrived. One student thought the notice had been wrong, but the observation had included its time. We added a later update without ____4____ (remove) the earlier one.

Keeping both entries helped us see the change more ____5____ (clear). It also reminded readers that a noticeboard cannot change by itself whenever the weather does. We decided ____6____ (check) it at two agreed times rather than promising constant updates.

The teacher thanked us ____7____ explaining the limits. Clear ____8____ (label) mattered as much as attractive lettering. A useful report did not need to claim more than its makers knew. For ____9____ (we), the project became ____10____ exercise in choosing words that matched the information available.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of prepare.
questions.explanation: Every morning establishes habit with singular a member, so prepares. Prepare disagrees and preparing lacks auxiliary.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Who/that is the human relative subject. Which is nonhuman, where not subject and whose requires a possessed noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of copy.
questions.explanation: Rather than copying is parallel with use in a contrast of methods; bare copy is also grammatical after the earlier verb structure. Copied is a finite past form incompatible with the habitual construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of remove.
questions.explanation: Without takes removing. Other listed forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of clear.
questions.explanation: Clearly modifies see. Clearness is noun; other unlisted readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of check.
questions.explanation: Decided takes to check. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Thanked us for explaining gives the action thanked. Other listed prepositions do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of label.
questions.explanation: Plural labels or the process nouns labelling/labeling both fit Clear ... mattered. Labelled is a participle, not the required noun subject.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: For takes object pronoun us. We is subject and our/ours possessive.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: An exercise uses an before a vowel sound. Other article readings remain reviewable.

materials.title: Standing beneath the arch
materials.text:
During a visit to a restored bridge, our class met an engineer who explained its stone arch. She began by asking us ____1____ (look) at the shape from the side. The stones were arranged so that forces could pass through the arch towards its supports.

We did not climb on the bridge or remove any part of it. Instead, the engineer used a small model ____2____ showed the arrangement on a table. When its temporary support was taken away correctly, the model remained standing.

I had expected the highest stone to do all the work. The demonstration made it ____3____ (easy) to understand the importance of the rest than a single photograph had. Each piece depended on the surrounding structure.

After ____4____ (watch), we tried arranging the model under supervision. Several ____5____ (attempt) failed because the pieces were not positioned properly. The engineer asked us to stop and examine the gaps rather than push harder.

Her explanation was about more than the stones. A real bridge also depends ____6____ the ground, its condition and the loads it carries. The small model helped with one idea; it was not a complete test of a full-sized structure.

Back at school, we described the visit ____7____ (careful). We wanted to distinguish what we had seen from conclusions we could not make. The engineer, ____8____ patience had helped us ask better questions, sent a short note checking our description. It was a ____9____ (remind) that an attractive demonstration can begin understanding without finishing it. We thanked her for giving ____10____ (we) that beginning.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of look.
questions.explanation: Asking us takes to look. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Model is subject antecedent of that/which showed. Who is human, where not subject and what does not follow this expressed antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of easy.
questions.explanation: Than a photograph had requires comparative easier or more easy. Plain, superlative and double comparative forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of watch.
questions.explanation: After takes watching in the prepositional clause. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of attempt.
questions.explanation: Several requires plural attempts. Attempt is singular and attempting an activity form rather than the numbered trials.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Depends on/upon names the supporting conditions. From/with/at do not complete depend here.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Carefully modifies described. Adjective careful and noun carefulness do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Whose supplies possession before patience in the non-defining clause. The other relatives do not fill that relation.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of remind.
questions.explanation: A reminder requires the singular noun naming something that prompts understanding. Remind is a verb and reminded a past/participle form.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Giving takes object us. We is subject and our/ours possessive.
